```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=TRUE,
                     fig.width=10, fig.height=8, dpi=130)
library(cmdstanr)
library(ggplot2)
library(data.table)
source(file.path(params$project_dir, "site_index_piecewise.R"))
run_dir <- file.path(params$project_dir, "si_fits_piecewise", params$run)
prepared <- readRDS(file.path(run_dir, "prepared.rds"))
fit <- readRDS(file.path(run_dir, "fit.rds"))
stopifnot(identical(prepared$model, "dd5_piecewise_smr"),
          !is.null(prepared$stan_data$P_share_centres))
object <- list(fit=fit, prepared=prepared)
d <- as.data.table(prepared$data)
priors <- as.data.frame(prepared$priors)
spp <- prepared$species
post <- as.matrix(fit$draws(variables=.si_pw_prediction_vars, format="matrix"))
object$draws <- post
set.seed(20261118)
ids <- sample.int(nrow(post), min(params$n_draws,nrow(post)))
grids <- list(DD5=seq(0,2500,length.out=151),
              VPD=seq(0,max(2.5,max(d$VPD)),length.out=151),
              CMD=seq(0,max(1600,max(d$CMD)),length.out=151))
prior_sim <- check_si_climate_piecewise_priors(
  priors, n_draws=params$n_draws, DD5_grid=grids$DD5,
  VPD_grid=grids$VPD, CMD_grid=grids$CMD, SMR=params$moisture,
  seed=87, plot=FALSE)
summarise_curve <- function(x,y,sp) {
  q <- t(apply(y,2,quantile,probs=c(.05,.5,.95),names=FALSE))
  data.frame(species=sp,x=x,lower=q[,1],median=q[,2],upper=q[,3])
}
curve_theme <- function() theme_bw(base_size=12) +
  theme(panel.grid.minor=element_blank(),strip.background=element_rect(fill="#edf2f5"))
curve_plot <- function(variable, prior=FALSE) {
  rows <- lapply(spp,function(sp) {
    if(prior) {
      y <- prior_sim$curves[[sp]][[variable]]
      if(variable=="CMD") y <- y[[1]]
    } else {
      nd <- data.frame(species=sp,DD5=params$DD5,VPD=params$VPD,
                       CMD=params$CMD,moisture=params$moisture,nutrient=params$nutrient)
      nd <- nd[rep(1,length(grids[[variable]])),]
      nd[[variable]] <- grids[[variable]]
      y <- draw_si_piecewise(object,nd,draw_ids=ids)
    }
    summarise_curve(grids[[variable]],y,sp)
  })
  tab <- rbindlist(rows)
  tab[,species:=factor(species,levels=spp)]
  rug <- data.frame(species=factor(d$species,levels=spp),x=d[[variable]])
  p <- ggplot(tab,aes(x,median)) +
    geom_ribbon(aes(ymin=lower,ymax=upper),fill="#0072B2",alpha=.18) +
    geom_line(colour="#0072B2",linewidth=.65) +
    facet_wrap(~species,ncol=3) + curve_theme() +
    labs(x=switch(variable,DD5="DD5 (degree-days)",VPD="Summer VPD (kPa)",CMD="CMD (mm)"),
         y=if(prior) "Climate multiplier" else "Expected site index (m)") +
    coord_cartesian(xlim=range(grids[[variable]]),
      ylim=if(prior) c(0,1) else c(0,max(35,5*ceiling(max(tab$upper)/5))))
  if(!prior) p <- p + geom_rug(data=rug,aes(x=x),inherit.aes=FALSE,
                               sides="b",alpha=.06)
  p
}

# Adjusted observations retain each draw's observed/predicted SI ratio.
# Align the horizontal axis for the explicit climate-by-SMR interactions.
adjust_climate_points <- function(variable, selected=c("Fd","Pl")) {
  obs <- as.data.frame(d[d$species %in% selected,])
  draws <- post[ids,,drop=FALSE]
  getv <- function(v,s) draws[,paste0(v,"[",s,"]")]
  ref_m <- (params$moisture-3)/3
  ref_n <- (match(params$nutrient,LETTERS[1:5])-3)/2
  logmu <- function(s,T,V,D,smr,n) {
    ramp <- pmin(1,pmax(0,T-200)/(getv("K_gap",s)*exp(getv("c_M",s)*(smr-3)/3)))
    # .si_pw_log_site accepts scalar CMD; the reference CMD may be draw-specific.
    site <- .si_pw_log_site(getv,s,n,smr,V,0)
    loss <- log(2)*(D/(getv("D50",s)*exp(getv("beta_CMD",s)*(smr-3)/3)))^getv("p_CMD",s)
    getv("log_P",s)+site-loss+
      log(getv("cold_floor",s)+(1-getv("cold_floor",s))*ramp)
  }
  out <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(obs)),function(i) {
    r <- obs[i,]; s <- match(r$species,spp); orig_m <- (r$moisture-3)/3
    x <- switch(variable,
      DD5=if(r$DD5<=200) rep(r$DD5,length(ids)) else
        200+(r$DD5-200)*exp(getv("c_M",s)*(ref_m-orig_m)),
      CMD=r$CMD*exp(getv("beta_CMD",s)*(ref_m-orig_m)),
      VPD=rep(r$VPD,length(ids)))
    actual <- logmu(s,r$DD5,r$VPD,r$CMD,r$moisture,(r$snr_numeric-3)/2)
    reference <- logmu(s,if(variable=="DD5") x else params$DD5,
      if(variable=="VPD") x else params$VPD,
      if(variable=="CMD") x else params$CMD,params$moisture,ref_n)
    log_adjusted <- log(r$site_index)+reference-actual
    stopifnot(all(is.finite(log_adjusted)),
      max(abs((log_adjusted-reference)-(log(r$site_index)-actual)))<1e-8)
    if(variable=="CMD") stopifnot(max(abs(
      x/(getv("D50",s)*exp(getv("beta_CMD",s)*ref_m))-
      r$CMD/(getv("D50",s)*exp(getv("beta_CMD",s)*orig_m))))<1e-8)
    data.frame(species=r$species,variable=variable,x=median(x),
               adjusted=exp(median(log_adjusted)))
  })
  result <- rbindlist(out)
  # Cross-check against the established DD5 adjustment implementation.
  if(variable=="DD5") {
    chk <- adjust_si_data_piecewise(object,data=obs[seq_len(min(6,nrow(obs))),],
      VPD=params$VPD,CMD=params$CMD,moisture=params$moisture,
      nutrient=params$nutrient,draw_ids=ids)
    stopifnot(max(abs(result$x[seq_len(nrow(chk))]-chk$DD5_aligned))<1e-8,
      max(abs(result$adjusted[seq_len(nrow(chk))]-chk$SI_adjusted))<1e-8)
  }
  result
}
overlay_plot <- function() {
  selected <- intersect(c("Fd","Pl"),spp)
  points <- rbindlist(lapply(names(grids),adjust_climate_points,selected=selected))
  curves <- rbindlist(lapply(names(grids),function(v) {
    rbindlist(lapply(selected,function(sp) {
      nd <- data.frame(species=sp,DD5=params$DD5,VPD=params$VPD,CMD=params$CMD,
                       moisture=params$moisture,nutrient=params$nutrient)
      nd <- nd[rep(1,length(grids[[v]])),]; nd[[v]] <- grids[[v]]
      tab <- summarise_curve(grids[[v]],draw_si_piecewise(object,nd,draw_ids=ids),sp)
      tab$variable <- v; tab
    }))
  }))
  # Zoom to the curve range; report all points outside the display explicitly.
  ymax <- max(35,5*ceiling(max(curves$upper)/5))
  counts <- points[,.(Total=.N,Outside_view=sum(x<min(grids[[.BY$variable]]) |
                x>max(grids[[.BY$variable]]) | adjusted>ymax)),by=.(species,variable)]
  visible <- points[x>=0 & adjusted<=ymax]
  visible <- visible[visible$x <= vapply(as.character(visible$variable),
                                         function(v) max(grids[[v]]),numeric(1))]
  lab <- c(DD5="DD5 aligned to reference SMR (degree-days)",
           VPD="Summer VPD (kPa)",CMD="CMD aligned to reference SMR (mm)")
  for(tab in list(curves,visible)) {
    tab[,variable:=factor(variable,levels=names(grids))]
    tab[,species:=factor(species,levels=selected)]
  }
  plot <- ggplot(curves,aes(x,median))+
    geom_ribbon(aes(ymin=lower,ymax=upper),fill="#0072B2",alpha=.18)+
    geom_point(data=visible,aes(x,adjusted),inherit.aes=FALSE,
               colour="#555555",alpha=.18,size=.65)+
    geom_line(colour="#0072B2",linewidth=.7)+
    facet_grid(species~variable,scales="free_x",labeller=labeller(variable=lab))+
    coord_cartesian(ylim=c(0,ymax))+curve_theme()+
    labs(x=NULL,y="Site index (m)",subtitle="Adjusted observations and conditional expected-SI curves")+
    theme(strip.text.x=element_text(size=8))
  list(plot=plot,counts=counts)
}
edatopic_plot <- function(DD5,VPD,CMD) {
  species <- intersect(c("Fd","Pl","Cw","Sx","Py","Ss"),spp)
  nd <- expand.grid(species=species,moisture=0:8,nutrient=LETTERS[1:5],
                    KEEP.OUT.ATTRS=FALSE,stringsAsFactors=FALSE)
  nd$DD5 <- DD5; nd$VPD <- VPD; nd$CMD <- CMD
  y <- draw_si_piecewise(object,nd,draw_ids=ids)
  q <- t(apply(y,2,quantile,c(.05,.5,.95),names=FALSE))
  nd$lower <- q[,1]; nd$median <- q[,2]; nd$upper <- q[,3]
  stopifnot(all(q>=0),all(q<=50))
  nd$species <- factor(nd$species,levels=species)
  nd$snr <- match(nd$nutrient,LETTERS[1:5])
  nd$label <- sprintf("%.1f\n[%.1f, %.1f]",nd$median,nd$lower,nd$upper)
  ggplot(nd,aes(snr,moisture,fill=median))+
    geom_tile(colour="white",linewidth=.3)+
    geom_text(aes(label=label,colour=median>25),size=2.35,lineheight=.95)+
    scale_colour_manual(values=c("FALSE"="#142b40","TRUE"="white"),guide="none")+
    scale_fill_gradient(low="#f1f7fb",high="#06466e",limits=c(0,50),name="SI (m)")+
    scale_x_continuous(breaks=1:5,labels=LETTERS[1:5],expand=c(0,0))+
    scale_y_reverse(breaks=0:8,expand=c(0,0))+
    coord_fixed()+facet_wrap(~species,ncol=3)+curve_theme()+
    labs(x="Soil nutrient regime",y="Soil moisture regime",
         subtitle=sprintf("DD5 %g | VPD %g kPa | CMD %g mm; median [90%% credible interval]",DD5,VPD,CMD))+
    theme(legend.position="bottom",panel.grid=element_blank())
}

bg_col <- intersect(c("BGC","bgc"),names(d))[1]

diag <- fit$diagnostic_summary()
```

## Model Summary

The model predicts **expected site index (SI, metres)** from species,
three climate variables, and soil moisture and nutrient regimes. It uses
a Bayesian hierarchy to share information among species while retaining
species-specific response curves. The current fit has **`r nrow(d)`
records and `r length(spp)` species**. It includes `r sum(bg)` rows in
BGC units beginning with BG (`r sum(bg & d$site_index < 5)` of these
have SI below 5 m). These rows supply direct evidence of productivity in
hot, dry environments; their incremental effect has not been quantified
by a matched before/after comparison here.

-   **DD5:** productivity rises approximately linearly above 200
    degree-days and reaches a species-specific plateau. Below 200 it has
    a small positive floor.
-   **Summer VPD:** a decreasing sigmoid represents atmospheric moisture
    stress.
-   **CMD:** a flexible decreasing exponential represents climatic water
    deficit.
-   **SMR (0--8):** productivity peaks at an estimated moisture optimum,
    with separate rates of decline toward the dry and wet extremes.
-   **SNR (A--E, coded 1--5):** a quadratic on the log scale allows an
    interior nutrient optimum, but does not require one.

Expected SI is bounded below 50 m at every site. Individual observations
retain lognormal residual variation and can exceed 50 m. BGC is retained
as a data label, **not a predictor or random effect**. PAS, DD18 and
Eref are not in this model.

### Hierarchy and interactions

| Component              | Structure                                                                            |
|:-----------------------------------|:-----------------------------------|
| Species                | Separate climate, edatopic, amplitude and residual parameters; most partially pooled |
| Cold floor             | Independent species priors in metres; not pooled                                     |
| DD5 × SMR              | SMR shifts the DD5 value where the plateau begins                                    |
| CMD × SMR              | SMR shifts the CMD giving a 50% drought multiplier                                   |
| Nutrient × moisture    | No explicit interaction; their baseline multipliers are separable                    |
| VPD × other predictors | No explicit interaction term                                                         |
| BGC / plot             | No BGC or plot-level random effects                                                  |

All components multiply on the SI scale, so the absolute effect of one
variable depends on the other multipliers even without an explicit
interaction parameter. SMR is a fixed site attribute in future
projections. Curves are fitted to spatial climate predictors and should
not automatically be interpreted as responses to individual-year weather
anomalies.

## Posterior climate curves {.tabset}

Lines are posterior medians of **expected SI**; ribbons are pointwise
90% credible intervals, not intervals for individual observations. Each
variable is varied while the others remain fixed at DD5 =
`r params$DD5`, VPD = `r params$VPD` kPa, CMD = `r params$CMD` mm, SMR =
`r params$moisture`, and SNR = `r params$nutrient`. Rugs show each
species' marginal observed climate values, not observations restricted
to these reference site conditions. Some plotted combinations are
outside the joint climate support of the data. The DD5 curve alone has
no warm decline: in future climates, declining growth arises through VPD
and CMD.


## Climate curves with adjusted observations

Fd and Pl fitting observations are adjusted draw by draw to the same
reference conditions used above, preserving their observed-to-expected
SI ratio:

$$Y_i^{\mathrm{adj},(b)}=Y_i\frac{\mu_{\mathrm{ref},i}^{(b)}}{\mu_{\mathrm{original},i}^{(b)}}.$$

To preserve the explicit SMR interactions, DD5 above 200 is aligned as
$200+(\mathrm{DD5}-200)\exp[c_s(m_{\mathrm{ref}}-m_i)]$; CMD is aligned
as $\mathrm{CMD}\exp[\beta_s(m_{\mathrm{ref}}-m_i)]$. VPD needs no
horizontal adjustment. Other climate predictors and soil conditions are
held at their reference values in each adjusted panel.

Points show posterior medians of the adjusted coordinates; their
adjustment uncertainty is not displayed. They are **model-adjusted
fitting observations**, not independent validation or raw measurements
at the reference site. Large adjustments can occur where original
expected SI is very low. The display is zoomed to the curves; counts of
points outside the displayed range are listed below.

```{r adjusted-observations, fig.width=12, fig.height=7}
overlays <- overlay_plot()
print(overlays$plot)
knitr::kable(overlays$counts)
```

## Edatopic examples {.tabset}

Each square cell gives posterior median expected SI and its pointwise
90% credible interval. All panels share the same 0--50 m colour scale.
These are conditional predictions, including for edatopic positions with
little or no data. The second climate setting is an illustrative
warmer/drier comparison, not a specified future scenario or BGC climate.

## Prior response curves {.tabset}

These curves simulate the **priors stored with this fit**, not the
current CSV. Lines and bands are marginal medians and pointwise 90%
prior intervals. They show climate multipliers, not full prior
predictive SI including residual variation. The DD5 prior panel uses SMR
3 (the reference knee); CMD uses SMR `r params$moisture`. The different
VPD centres and widths encode species-specific prior knowledge. Very
narrow bands can reflect strong prior constraints.

### Amplitude and edatopic priors

The amplitude and edatopic prior settings are identical across species
in this fit. The following panels illustrate them using
`r spp[1]`. The floor and plateau are in metres; soil responses are
dimensionless multipliers.

```{r prior-soil, fig.height=6}
ed <- check_si_piecewise_priors(priors,n_draws=params$n_draws,plot=FALSE,seed=88)
v <- prior_sim$parameter_draws[[spp[1]]]
e <- ed$parameter_draws[[spp[1]]]
smr <- seq(0,8,length.out=151)
snr <- seq(1,5,length.out=151)
fm <- sapply(smr,function(x) exp(ifelse(x<e$O_M,
  log(e$r0)*((x-e$O_M)/e$O_M)^2,
  log(e$r8)*((x-e$O_M)/(8-e$O_M))^2)))
a <- e$b_NN-log(e$rA); b <- e$b_NN
qm <- pmax(b-a,b+a); inside <- b<0 & abs(a)< -2*b
qm[inside] <- -a[inside]^2/(4*b[inside])
fn <- sapply(snr,function(x) { n <- (x-3)/2; exp(a*n+b*n^2-qm) })
old <- par(mfrow=c(2,2),mar=c(4,4,2,1))
hist(v[,"F_m"],breaks=35,col="#cde3ef",border="white",main="Cold floor prior",xlab="F (m)")
hist(v[,"P"],breaks=35,col="#cde3ef",border="white",main="Plateau prior",xlab="P (m)",xlim=c(0,50))
panel <- function(x,y,label) {
 q <- apply(y,2,quantile,c(.05,.5,.95))
 plot(x,q[2,],type="n",ylim=c(0,1),xlab=label,ylab="Multiplier")
 polygon(c(x,rev(x)),c(q[1,],rev(q[3,])),col="#cde3ef",border=NA)
 lines(x,q[2,],col="#0072B2",lwd=2)
}
panel(smr,fm,"SMR"); panel(snr,fn,"SNR (1=A, ..., 5=E)")
par(old)
```

## Mathematical specification

For observation $i$ of species $s$, write $T=\mathrm{DD5}$,
$V=\mathrm{VPD}$, $D=\mathrm{CMD}$, $x=\mathrm{SMR}$, $m=(x-3)/3$, and
$n=(\mathrm{SNR}-3)/2$.

$$
Y_i\sim\operatorname{Lognormal}\left(\log\mu_i-\tfrac12\sigma_s^2,\sigma_s\right),
\qquad
\mu_i=H_s(T,x)\,M_s(x)\,N_s(n)\,V_s(V)\,D_s(D,x).
$$

This parameterisation makes $E[Y_i\mid\theta]=\mu_i$. The residual log
SD $\sigma_s$ varies by species, not by climate.

### Climate components

With $0<F_s<P_s<50$ and $G_s>0$,

$$
K_s(x)=200+G_s e^{c_s m},\qquad
u_s(T,x)=\min\left(1,\frac{\max(0,T-200)}{G_s e^{c_s m}}\right),
\qquad H_s(T,x)=F_s+(P_s-F_s)u_s(T,x).
$$

$F_s$ and $P_s$ are the floor and plateau **before** soil and drought
reductions. $K_s(3)=200+G_s$ is the reference DD5 knee. The curve is
continuous with corners at 200 and $K_s(x)$.

$$
V_s(V)=\operatorname{logit}^{-1}\left(\frac{V50_s-V}{w_s}\right),\qquad
D_s(D,x)=\exp\left[-\log(2)\left(\frac{D}{D50_s e^{\beta_s m}}\right)^{p_s}\right].
$$

$V50_s$ is the VPD where its multiplier is 0.5; $w_s>0$ controls decline
width. $D50_s$ is the corresponding CMD at SMR 3; $p_s>0$ controls
curvature. Positive $\beta_s$ means moister sites tolerate greater CMD.
Its sign is estimated.

### Edatopic components

$$
\log M_s(x)=
\begin{cases}
\log r_{0s}\left(\dfrac{x-O_s}{O_s}\right)^2,&x<O_s,\\
\log r_{8s}\left(\dfrac{x-O_s}{8-O_s}\right)^2,&x\ge O_s.
\end{cases}
$$

$O_s\in(0,8)$ is the baseline moisture optimum; $r_{0s},r_{8s}\in(0,1)$
are productivity ratios at SMR 0 and 8 relative to that optimum.
Climate--SMR interactions can shift the optimum of the complete SI
surface away from $O_s$.

$$
q_s(n)=(b_s-\log r_{As})n+b_s n^2,\qquad
N_s(n)=\exp\left[q_s(n)-\max_{z\in[-1,1]}q_s(z)\right].
$$

$r_{As}$ is the A:C productivity ratio; $b_s$ is nutrient curvature.
Normalising by the continuous maximum ensures $N_s\le1$. All four
multipliers are at most one, hence $\mu_i\le P_s<50$.

### Partial pooling and priors

Most parameters use a shared-deviation hierarchy on their working scale:

$$
\theta_{sj}=a_{sj}+b_{sj}
\left(\sqrt{\rho_j}\,\delta_j+\sqrt{1-\rho_j}\,z_{sj}\right),
\quad \delta_j,z_{sj}\sim N(0,1),\quad\rho_j\sim\operatorname{Beta}(2,2).
$$

$a_{sj}$ and $b_{sj}$ are the supplied species prior centre and SD. The
shared deviation allows species to inform one another while preserving
each supplied marginal normal prior. This is applied separately to
$\log G,\log V50,\log w,\log D50,\log p,\beta$ and the five edatopic
working parameters
$\operatorname{logit}(O/8),\operatorname{logit}(r_0), \operatorname{logit}(r_8),\log r_A,b$.
Sharing is across species, with no taxonomic or coastal/interior
grouping.

The cold floor has an independent normal prior on
$\operatorname{logit}(F_s/50)$. The plateau uses the shared hierarchy
for $h_s$, with $P_s=F_s+(50-F_s)\operatorname{logit}^{-1}(h_s)$. Its
prior centre is calibrated to the supplied plateau median conditional on
$F_s$ equalling its prior median.

The two remaining hierarchies are

$$
\begin{aligned}
c_s&=\bar c+\tau_c z_s,&\bar c&\sim N(0,0.15^2),&\tau_c&\sim\mathrm{HalfNormal}(0.10),\\
\log\sigma_s&=\ell+\tau_\sigma z'_s,&\ell&\sim N(\log0.25,0.5^2),&
\tau_\sigma&\sim\mathrm{HalfNormal}(0.35),
\end{aligned}
$$

with independent standard-normal $z_s,z'_s$.

## Fit checks and provenance

```{r diagnostic-table}
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  Chain=seq_along(diag$num_divergent),
  Divergences=diag$num_divergent,
  Treedepth_hits=diag$num_max_treedepth,
  E_BFMI=round(diag$ebfmi,3)))
```

Among the response parameters and selected hyperparameters checked here,
maximum R-hat is `r sprintf('%.4f',max(ds$rhat,na.rm=TRUE))`, minimum
bulk ESS is `r round(min(ds$ess_bulk,na.rm=TRUE))`, and minimum tail ESS
is `r round(min(ds$ess_tail,na.rm=TRUE))`. These sampler checks do not
establish predictive accuracy or reliable extrapolation. This report
does not perform held-out validation or refit the model.

```{r species-counts}
counts <- d[,.(Records=.N,Minimum_SI=min(site_index),Maximum_SI=max(site_index)),by=species]
knitr::kable(counts,digits=2)
```

Saved run: **`r params$run`**. Priors and fitting observations come from
its `prepared.rds`; posterior draws come from its `fit.rds`. The model
equations were checked against the current `site_index_piecewise.stan`
and plotting calculations use `site_index_piecewise.R`. These source
files are not archived inside the saved fit folder; keep their versions
with the report for reproducibility.

```{r prior-table}
knitr::kable(priors,digits=4)
```

</details>

### Re-rendering

This document only reads the saved fit. Change `params$run` to select
another run, or override reference climate and edatopic conditions when
rendering:

```{r render-example, eval=FALSE, echo=TRUE}
rmarkdown::render(
  "piecewise_report.Rmd",
  params=list(run="run_3e2816037ba5",moisture=4,nutrient="C",
              DD5=2000,VPD=0.6,CMD=200)
)
```

Requires R packages cmdstanr, posterior (through cmdstanr), data.table,
ggplot2, knitr and rmarkdown, plus Pandoc (provided by RStudio or
Quarto).
